skill.name: request-refactor-plan
skill.description: Plan refactors by interviewing the user, checking repository context, splitting work into tiny commits, and drafting a GitHub issue.
skill.summary: Create a repository-aware refactor plan with scoped decisions, test notes, and tiny commits.
skill.author: mattpocock

security_audit.summary: Static analysis found no suspicious patterns and produced no static findings to adjudicate. Manual review found a prompt-only workflow for refactor planning, repository review, test planning, and GitHub issue drafting. No prompt injection attempt or malicious intent was found.

content.value_statement: Large refactors are risky when goals, scope, and test strategy are unclear. This skill turns a refactor idea into a reviewable GitHub issue with tiny commits and explicit decisions.
actual_capabilities: Interviews the user to define the refactor problem, goals, constraints, and solution options.
Checks the repository to compare user assumptions with the current codebase.
Breaks implementation work into small commits that should keep the project working.
Captures implementation decisions, interfaces, schema changes, and API contracts in a decision document.
Identifies relevant test coverage and records testing decisions.
Drafts a GitHub issue using the included refactor plan template.
limitations: It does not perform the refactor itself.
GitHub issue creation requires available GitHub tools, repository access, and user approval.
Plans depend on accurate repository context and detailed user answers.
It avoids file paths and code snippets in the final issue because they can become stale.

use_cases.title: Plan a risky backend refactor
use_cases.description: Define the problem, compare options, and split backend changes into small commits before implementation starts.

use_cases.title: Coordinate technical debt work
use_cases.description: Turn a broad cleanup request into scoped decisions, testing notes, and reviewable delivery steps.

use_cases.title: Prepare a public issue
use_cases.description: Create clear GitHub issue text that explains the refactor plan without brittle file paths or code snippets.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a small refactor
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request with a known problem.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to help me plan a refactor. The problem is [describe problem]. Ask me questions before drafting the plan.

prompt_templates.title: Compare solution options
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request with multiple possible approaches.
prompt_templates.prompt: I want to refactor [area]. Please inspect the repository, check my assumptions, present other options, and help me choose a scoped approach.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a refactoring RFC
prompt_templates.scenario: Team planning request before work begins.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a refactoring RFC for [goal]. Interview me about constraints, interfaces, schema changes, API contracts, testing, and out-of-scope work.

prompt_templates.title: Create a GitHub issue plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for a final issue draft.
prompt_templates.prompt: Build the full refactor plan for [project area]. Explore the repo, challenge assumptions, define tiny commits, capture decisions, and draft the GitHub issue.

output_examples.input: A developer wants to replace duplicate validation logic across several modules.
output_examples.output: The skill produces a problem statement, selected approach, tiny commit sequence, decision document, testing decisions, and out-of-scope items.

output_examples.input: A technical lead needs an RFC for moving API response formatting into a shared layer.
output_examples.output: The skill asks architecture questions, compares alternatives, records selected contracts, and drafts issue-ready planning text.

output_examples.input: A maintainer wants to split a large refactor into reviewable work.
output_examples.output: The skill maps incremental commits that preserve behavior and points to existing test patterns.

best_practices: Give a full problem description, known constraints, and suspected root causes.
Answer scope questions before asking for the final GitHub issue text.
Confirm testing strategy and excluded work before implementation begins.
anti_patterns: Using the skill to skip design review for a risky architecture change.
Requesting implementation code before the refactor plan is agreed.
Leaving goals vague, such as improve quality across the whole codebase.

faq.question: Does this skill change my code?
faq.answer: No. It creates a plan and issue text. Any code changes require a separate implementation request.

faq.question: Can it create the GitHub issue for me?
faq.answer: Yes, when GitHub tools and repository permissions are available. You should review the issue text before submission.

faq.question: Why does it ask many questions?
faq.answer: Refactors fail when scope is unclear. The interview helps define decisions, risks, testing, and excluded work.

faq.question: Will the final issue include file paths?
faq.answer: No. The skill instructs the assistant to avoid file paths and code snippets because they can become stale.

faq.question: How small are the commits?
faq.answer: The plan aims for commits that keep the project working after each step.

faq.question: Can it evaluate test coverage?
faq.answer: It can inspect existing tests and summarize coverage gaps. It cannot guarantee complete coverage without project-specific review.
